title: Vishnu Sahasranama: Why Millions Chant It and How to Begin
intro: The Vishnu Sahasranama is a list of a thousand names of Vishnu, found in the Mahabharata. It is recited daily in many homes and temples.

p: It is part of the Anushasana Parva of the Mahabharata. Bhishma, lying on his bed of arrows, recites the thousand names to Yudhishthira in answer to his questions about the best way to find peace.
Each name describes a quality of God, such as Keshava, Govinda or Madhava. Reciting them is believed to bring peace of mind, and many people say it brings steadiness in difficult times.

Start by listening to a clear recording and following along with the text in your own script. Learn it in small parts, a few verses a day. Even reciting the shorter Vishnu Gayatri and the closing verses is a good start.
Early morning, evenings, Ekadashi, and Thursdays are popular. Consistency matters more than the time.

faq.a: A complete recitation takes roughly 25 to 30 minutes.
It takes practice, but listening and repeating daily helps a lot.
